title_en: Rules on Supervision of Civil Proceedings by People's Procuratorates

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Rules are formulated in order to safeguard and regulate the People's Procuratorate's performance of civil procuratorial duties according to law, in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Organic Law of the People's Procuratorates of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant provisions, and in light of the actual work of the People's Procuratorate.

Article 2 The People's Procuratorate shall independently exercise its procuratorial power according to law, and by handling cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, it shall uphold judicial fairness and judicial authority, safeguard national interests and social public interests, protect the lawful rights and interests of natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations, and ensure the uniform and correct implementation of national laws.
Article 3 The People's Procuratorate shall exercise legal supervision over civil action activities by means of protests, procuratorial proposals, and other means.

Article 4 When handling cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, the People's Procuratorate shall base itself on facts and take law as the criterion, adhere to the principles of openness, fairness, justice, and good faith, respect and protect the litigation rights of the parties, and supervise and support the People's Court in lawfully exercising its adjudicative and enforcement powers.

Article 5 The departments responsible for complaint and petition procuratorial work, civil procuratorial work, and case management shall respectively undertake the acceptance, handling, and management of cases concerning the supervision of civil actions. The various departments shall cooperate with and check each other.

Article 6 When handling cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, the People's Procuratorate shall implement a procurator case-handling responsibility system, under which the procurator, the chief procurator, and the procuratorial committee shall make decisions on case-handling matters within their respective scope of functions and powers, and shall bear corresponding judicial responsibility in accordance with the provisions.

Article 7 When handling cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, the People's Procuratorate may, based on the circumstances of the case, have a single procurator handle the case alone, or have a case-handling group composed of two or more procurators handle the case. Where the case is handled by a procurator case-handling group, the chief procurator shall designate one procurator as the lead procurator to organize and direct the case-handling group in handling the case.
When handling a case, a procurator may, as necessary, be assisted by procuratorial assistants such as assistant procurators, clerks, judicial police, and procuratorial technical personnel. Procuratorial assistants shall undertake corresponding procuratorial assistance matters in accordance with the relevant provisions.

Article 8 The Supreme People's Procuratorate shall lead the civil action supervision work of local People's Procuratorates at all levels and special People's Procuratorates; a higher People's Procuratorate shall lead the civil action supervision work of a lower People's Procuratorate.
Where a higher People's Procuratorate considers a decision of a lower People's Procuratorate to be erroneous, it shall have the power to instruct the lower People's Procuratorate to correct it, or to revoke or modify it according to law. The decision of the higher People's Procuratorate shall be made in writing, and the lower People's Procuratorate shall execute it. Where a lower People's Procuratorate has a different opinion on the decision of the higher People's Procuratorate, it may report to the higher People's Procuratorate while executing the decision.
A higher People's Procuratorate may, according to law, uniformly deploy procuratorial personnel within its jurisdiction to handle cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, and the decision for such deployment shall be made in writing. The deployed procurator may represent the People's Procuratorate handling the case in performing the relevant procuratorial duties.

Article 9 The chief procurator of the People's Procuratorate, or a deputy chief procurator authorized by the chief procurator, may, in accordance with the relevant provisions, attend as a non-voting participant the meeting of the adjudication committee of the People's Court at the same level when it discusses civil protest cases or other topics related to civil action supervision work.
Article 10 When handling cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, the People's Procuratorate shall implement a system of withdrawal.

Article 11 When handling cases concerning the supervision of civil actions, procuratorial personnel shall uphold an objective and impartial position and consciously accept supervision.
Procuratorial personnel shall not accept invitations to dinner, gifts, or other benefits from the parties, their litigation agents, specific persons with a relationship, or intermediary organizations, nor shall they meet with the parties or persons entrusted by them in violation of the provisions.
Where procuratorial personnel engage in acts such as accepting bribes or bending the law for personal gain, they shall be subject to disciplinary liability and legal liability.
Procuratorial personnel shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions, comprehensively, truthfully, and timely record and report acts concerning the inquiry, intervention, or interference in the handling of cases concerning the supervision of civil actions or other significant matters.

Article 12 Where a procuratorial personnel has any of the circumstances specified in Article 44 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, he or she shall withdraw on his or her own motion, and the parties shall have the right to apply for his or her withdrawal.
The provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply to clerks, interpreters, expert evaluators, and inspectors.

Article 13 Where a procuratorial personnel withdraws on his or her own motion, he or she may do so orally or in writing, and shall state the reasons. Where the application is made orally, it shall be recorded in the file.

Article 14 A party applying for withdrawal shall do so orally or in writing before the People's Procuratorate makes a decision on whether to file a protest or a procuratorial proposal, and shall state the reasons. Where the application is made orally, it shall be recorded in the file. Where the application for withdrawal is made pursuant to paragraph 2 of Article 44 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, relevant evidence shall be provided.
The person whose withdrawal is applied for shall suspend participation in the work of the case before the People's Procuratorate decides whether to approve the withdrawal, unless urgent measures are required for the case.

Article 15 Where a procuratorial personnel has a circumstance requiring withdrawal but has not withdrawn on his or her own motion and the parties have not applied for his or her withdrawal, the chief procurator or the procuratorial committee shall decide on his or her withdrawal.

Article 16 The withdrawal of the chief procurator shall be discussed and decided by the procuratorial committee; the withdrawal of procuratorial personnel and other personnel shall be decided by the chief procurator. When the procuratorial committee discusses the withdrawal of the chief procurator, the deputy chief procurator shall preside, and the chief procurator shall not participate.

Article 17 The People's Procuratorate shall, within three days, make a decision on a party's application for withdrawal and notify the applicant. If the applicant is dissatisfied with the decision, he or she may, at the time of receiving the decision, apply for reconsideration to the original deciding organ once. The People's Procuratorate shall, within three days, make a reconsideration decision and notify the reconsideration applicant. During the period of reconsideration, the person whose withdrawal is applied for shall not suspend participation in the work of the case.

Article 20 Where a party applies to the People's Procuratorate for supervision pursuant to subparagraph (1) of Article 19 of these Rules, the application shall be filed within two years from the date the People's Court renders a ruling rejecting the application for retrial or the date the retrial judgment or ruling takes legal effect.
The time period provided for in this Article is an unchangeable period, and the provisions on suspension, interruption, and extension shall not apply.
Cases in which the People's Procuratorate initiates the supervision procedure ex officio shall not be subject to the time limit provided for in paragraph 1 of this Article.

Article 21 A party who applies to a People's Procuratorate for supervision shall submit an application for supervision, identification documents, relevant legal instruments, and evidentiary materials. If evidentiary materials are submitted, a list of evidence shall be attached.
If the materials for the supervision application are incomplete, the People's Procuratorate shall require the applicant to complete them within a specified period and shall clearly inform the applicant of all the materials to be completed at one time. If the applicant fails to complete them within the specified period, the supervision application shall be deemed withdrawn.

Article 23 The identification documents as specified in Article 21 of these Rules include:
(1) for a natural person, his or her resident identity card, military officer card, soldier card, passport, or other valid documents capable of proving his or her identity;
(2) for a legal person or an unincorporated organization, its unified social credit code certificate, business license copy, organization code certificate, and the identification documents of its legal representative or principal responsible person, or other valid certificates.
After verifying and confirming that the identification documents submitted by the party are correct, the People's Procuratorate shall retain copies.

Article 24 The relevant legal instruments as specified in Article 21 of these Rules refer to all judgments, rulings, decisions, mediation statements, and other legal instruments made by the People's Court during the litigation of the case.
Article 25 A party applying for supervision may appoint a litigation agent in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 29 If a party applies to a People's Procuratorate for a procuratorial recommendation or a protest pursuant to paragraph 1 of Article 209 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the application shall be accepted by the department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that rendered the effective civil judgment, ruling, or mediation statement.
If the People's Court renders a ruling dismissing the retrial application or fails to render a ruling on the retrial application within the time limit, and the party applies to the People's Procuratorate for supervision, the application shall be accepted by the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that rendered the original effective civil judgment, ruling, or mediation statement.

Article 30 If a party believes that an adjudicator has engaged in illegal acts in civil adjudication procedures or that there are illegal circumstances in civil enforcement activities, and applies to a People's Procuratorate for supervision, the application shall be accepted by the department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that tried or enforced the case.
If a party is dissatisfied with a reconsideration ruling, decision, or other act made by a higher People's Court and files a supervision application, the application shall be accepted by the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the higher People's Court. After acceptance, the People's Procuratorate may, as needed and in accordance with the relevant provisions of these Rules, refer the case to the People's Procuratorate at the same level as the People's Court that originally tried or enforced the case for handling.

Article 31 If a party believes that a People's Procuratorate has failed to accept its supervision application according to law, it may apply to the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level for supervision. If the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level considers that the party's supervision application meets the conditions for acceptance, it shall instruct the lower-level People's Procuratorate to accept it, or it may directly accept it when necessary.

Article 33 The department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work shall, within three days from the date of deciding to accept, prepare a Notice of Acceptance, send it to the applicant, and inform the applicant of his or her rights and obligations; at the same time, it shall send the Notice of Acceptance and a copy of the application for supervision to the other parties and inform them of their rights and obligations. The other parties may submit written opinions within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the copy of the application for supervision; failure to submit opinions shall not affect the People's Procuratorate's examination of the case.

Article 34 The department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work shall, within three days from the date of deciding to accept, transfer the case materials to the department in charge of civil procuratorial work of this Procuratorate, and simultaneously send a copy of the Notice of Acceptance to the department in charge of case management of this Procuratorate. If the department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work receives written opinions or other materials submitted by other parties, it shall promptly transfer them to the department in charge of civil procuratorial work.

Article 35 If a natural person, legal person, or unincorporated organization other than a party believes that an adjudicator has engaged in illegal acts in the civil adjudication procedures of a People's Court or that there are illegal circumstances in civil enforcement activities, they may file a complaint with the People's Procuratorate at the same level. The complaint shall be accepted by the department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work of the People's Procuratorate.
The department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work shall handle the received complaint in accordance with the Provisions on the Work of Complaints and Petitions of the People's Procuratorate and other relevant provisions.

Article 36 The department in charge of complaint and petition procuratorial work may, in accordance with the Provisions on the Work of Complaints and Petitions of the People's Procuratorate, assign petition cases involving supervision of civil actions to lower-level People's Procuratorates for handling.

Article 38 Cases in which a lower-level People's Procuratorate requests a protest or requests other supervision from a higher-level People's Procuratorate shall be accepted by the department in charge of case management of the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level.
For a civil action supervision case in which supervision procedures are initiated ex officio, the department in charge of civil procuratorial work shall register and have it accepted by the department in charge of case management.

Article 39 After receiving the case materials, the department in charge of case management shall register the case within three days and transfer the case materials and the case registration form to the department in charge of civil procuratorial work; if the case materials do not conform to the requirements, it shall require that they be supplemented.
After the department in charge of case management has registered and accepted the case, if it is necessary to notify the parties, the department in charge of civil procuratorial work shall prepare a Notice of Acceptance and send it to the parties within three days.
Article 99 The provisions of paragraph 3 of Article 208 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply to judges, people's assessors, judge assistants, and clerks.

Article 101 Where a People's Procuratorate discovers that, in the civil adjudication procedure of the people's court at the same level, an adjudicator has committed an illegal act as specified in Article 46 of the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China and such act may affect the fair adjudication or enforcement of the case, it shall issue a procuratorial recommendation to the people's court at the same level.

Article 102 Where a People's Procuratorate issues a procuratorial recommendation in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter, it shall prepare a Procuratorial Recommendation Letter, and within fifteen days from the date of the decision to issue the procuratorial recommendation, transfer the Procuratorial Recommendation Letter together with the case file to the people's court at the same level, and prepare a Notice of the decision to issue the procuratorial recommendation and send it to the applicant.

Article 103 Where a People's Procuratorate considers that the grounds for ascertaining the illegal acts of adjudicators in the adjudication procedure subject to supervision applied by the party are insufficient, it shall decide not to support the supervision application, and within fifteen days from the date of the decision, prepare a Decision on Not Supporting the Supervision Application and send it to the applicant.

Article 104 A People's Procuratorate shall exercise legal supervision over the activities of a people's court in enforcing effective civil judgments, rulings, mediation agreements, payment orders, arbitration awards, notarized creditor's rights documents and other legal instruments.

Article 105 Where a People's Procuratorate considers that a people's court may be negligent in performing its duties in enforcement activities, it may, in accordance with the relevant provisions, issue a Notice on Explaining the Enforcement Circumstances of the Case to the people's court, requiring an explanation of the enforcement circumstances and reasons of the case.

Article 107 Where a case is transferred for handling after acceptance by a People's Procuratorate in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 30 of these Rules, and the lower-level People's Procuratorate, upon review, considers that the enforcement reconsideration ruling, decision, etc. made by the people's court is illegal or erroneous, it shall request the higher-level People's Procuratorate to supervise; if it considers that the enforcement reconsideration ruling, decision, etc. made by the people's court is correct, it shall decide not to support the supervision application.

Article 108 Where a People's Procuratorate issues a procuratorial recommendation on enforcement activities, it shall be decided by the chief procurator or the procuratorial committee, prepare a Procuratorial Recommendation Letter, and within fifteen days from the date of the decision, transfer the Procuratorial Recommendation Letter together with the case file to the people's court at the same level, and prepare a Notice of the decision to issue the procuratorial recommendation and send it to the parties.

Article 109 Where a People's Procuratorate considers that there is no illegal circumstance in the enforcement activities of the people's court subject to supervision applied by the party, it shall decide not to support the supervision application, and within fifteen days from the date of the decision, prepare a Decision on Not Supporting the Supervision Application and send it to the applicant.

Article 110 Where a People's Procuratorate discovers that an enforcement officer has committed an illegal act in the enforcement activities of the people's court at the same level, it shall implement the relevant provisions of Chapter VI of these Rules mutatis mutandis.

Article 111 The department responsible for case management of a People's Procuratorate shall manage, supervise, and provide early warning regarding the acceptance, time limits, procedures, quality, etc. of civil action supervision cases.

Article 113 The department responsible for case management shall exercise supervision and management over the preparation and issuance of civil action supervision legal documents in the name of the procuratorate.

Article 114 For a civil action supervision case handled by a People's Procuratorate, if after the case is concluded, it is necessary to transfer case materials to another unit, the department responsible for case management shall uniformly review whether the transferred materials are standardized and complete. If the department responsible for case management considers that the materials are standardized, complete, and meet the conditions for transfer, the case-handling department shall immediately transfer them in accordance with the provisions; if it considers that the materials do not meet the requirements, it shall promptly notify the case-handling department to supplement or correct them.

Article 115 The legal instruments such as civil judgments, rulings or mediation agreements served by the people's court to the People's Procuratorate shall be received by the department responsible for case management, which shall promptly register and transfer them to the department responsible for civil procuratorial work.

Article 116 During the process of handling a civil action supervision case by the People's Procuratorate, if a party or its litigation agent submits any application, request or written materials, they shall be received by the department responsible for case management, and if relevant formalities need to be issued, the department responsible for case management shall issue them. After receiving the materials, the department responsible for case management shall promptly transfer them to the department responsible for civil procuratorial work.

Article 118 Where the new evidence submitted by the applicant to the People's Procuratorate is forged, or the applicant makes a false statement on important facts of the case, the People's Procuratorate shall criticize and educate the applicant, and may terminate the review, unless supervision is truly necessary; if the act is suspected of disciplinary or criminal violations, it shall be transferred to the relevant authority for handling in accordance with the provisions.
Where another party has the circumstances specified in the preceding paragraph, the People's Procuratorate shall criticize and educate such party; if the act is suspected of disciplinary or criminal violations, it shall be transferred to the relevant authority for handling in accordance with the provisions.

Article 119 Where a People's Procuratorate discovers that a People's Court has illegal or erroneous circumstances in reviewing and handling a party's application for enforcement, application for revocation of an arbitral award, or application for enforcement of a notarized creditor's right document, it shall handle the matter by reference to the relevant provisions of Chapters VI and VII of these Rules.

Article 120 The department responsible for civil procuratorial work, in the course of performing its duties, discovers acts suspected of violating discipline or committing crimes, and acts requiring the investigation of judicial responsibility, shall report to the Chief Procurator for a decision, and promptly transfer the relevant clues and materials to the organ or department with jurisdiction.
Where other functional departments of the People's Procuratorate, in the course of performing their duties, discover clues to civil litigation supervision cases that, in accordance with these Rules, shall be initiated ex officio, they shall promptly notify the department responsible for civil procuratorial work.

Article 121 Where a People's Procuratorate discovers that a relevant decision it has made is indeed erroneous and needs to be corrected, or there are other circumstances requiring withdrawal, it shall be decided by the Chief Procurator or the Procuratorial Committee of that People's Procuratorate.

Article 122 Where a People's Court makes a suggestion regarding the supervisory conduct of a People's Procuratorate, the People's Procuratorate shall reply in writing to the People's Court with the result of its handling within one month. Where the People's Court disagrees with the reply and raises the matter through the People's Court at the next higher level to the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level, and the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level considers the People's Court's suggestion to be correct, it shall require the lower-level People's Procuratorate to make corrections promptly.

Article 123 After a People's Court makes a retrial judgment, ruling, or other handling decision on a civil litigation supervision case, the People's Procuratorate that issued the supervision opinion shall review the handling result and fill out the Registration Form for Review of Handling Results of Civil Litigation Supervision Cases.

Article 125 Local People's Procuratorates at all levels may request instructions from the People's Procuratorate at the next higher level regarding major civil litigation supervision cases where the application of law is indeed difficult and complex and the procuratorate itself finds it difficult to decide.
Cases requiring instructions shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Procuratorate on handling request documents submitted by lower-level People's Procuratorates and on the submission of official documents by lower-level People's Procuratorates to the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 127 The preparation of legal documents for civil litigation supervision shall conform to the prescribed formats.
The formats of legal documents for civil litigation supervision shall be separately formulated.
Article 128 A People's Procuratorate may send legal documents by reference to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
Article 129 Where a People's Procuratorate discovers clerical errors in a legal document it has prepared, it shall make a Correction Decision to make corrections.
Article 130 A People's Procuratorate handling a civil litigation supervision case shall establish a civil litigation supervision case file in accordance with the provisions.

Article 131 When handling a civil litigation supervision case, a People's Procuratorate shall not charge a case acceptance fee. The expenses incurred from applying for photocopying, expert evaluation, audit, inspection, etc., shall be paid directly by the applicant to the relevant institution or unit, and the People's Procuratorate shall not collect or pay on behalf of others.
Article 132 For the handling of procuratorial suggestion cases, if these Rules do not provide otherwise, the Provisions of the People's Procuratorate on Procuratorial Suggestion Work shall apply.

Article 133 For the handling of civil public interest litigation supervision cases, these Rules and the relevant judicial interpretations of the procuratorate on public interest litigation shall apply.

Article 134 For the handling of civil litigation supervision cases by special People's Procuratorates such as military procuratorates, and for the handling of civil litigation supervision cases by People's Procuratorates against other special People's Courts, these Rules and other relevant provisions shall apply.

Article 135 These Rules shall come into force as of August 1, 2021, and the Rules of the People's Procuratorate on Civil Litigation Supervision (for Trial Implementation) shall be abolished simultaneously. If any other provisions previously published by this Procuratorate are inconsistent with these Rules, these Rules shall prevail.
Main distribution: All levels of People's Procuratorates.
Copy to: Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission, Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress;
Leaders of this Procuratorate, full-time members of the Procuratorial Committee;
All internal organs and directly affiliated institutions.
